<reason>CON won a competitive definitional clash: the motion’s “because expensive/performative, therefore little obligation to traditional expectations” is a non sequitur unless those expectations are the commercial script. CON kept a live, usable test (old, cross-cultural, enactment vs display), treated vows/witnesses/family/meal as still owed, and parked expense on a parasite rather than the host. PRO’s lived-enforcement reading was rhetorically closer to ordinary wedding pressure but stayed circular and inconsistent (diamond as marketing, guest list as tradition), so it never cleanly carried “little obligation” to tradition as such.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R2 circularity turn: if tradition is whatever is enforced under that name, the motion collapses into a claim about pressure, contradicts PRO calling the equally enforced diamond “marketing,” and cannot even privilege PRO’s own small-wedding alternatives.</best_rebuttal>
